chunks: And from the hadith of Yazeed ibn Sinan, who said: Abur-Rabee' az-Zahrani narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, saying: Mujalid ibn Sa'eed narrated to us, from ash-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Samra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave us a speech and I heard him saying: 'This matter will remain strong, dominant, and prevailing over its opponents until twelve (leaders) rule, all of them...'

Then the people began talking and making noise, so I could not understand what he said after 'all of them'. I asked my father, 'O my father, what did he say after 'all of them'? He said: He said: 'All of them are from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and lineage of the future leaders of Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by al-Nu'mani, establishes the number and tribal origin of the twelve Imams, affirming the Qurayshi lineage as a non-negotiable criterion for leadership in both Sunni and Shia traditions. The clarification that 'all of them' are from Quraysh underscores the continuity of authority within the Prophet's tribe, reinforcing the theological basis for the Imamate's legitimacy and political supremacy.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (19) Yazeed bin Sinan narrated from Abur-Rabee’ az-Zahrani from Hammad bin Zayd from Mujalid bin Sa’eed from ash-Shi’bi that Jabir bin Samra had said: Once the Prophet (S) made a speech before us and I heard him saying: “This matter (the religion) will remain strong and prevailing over its opponents until twelve (caliphs) will have ruled. All of them…”

Then people began talking and I could not understand what the Prophet (S) had said after “all of them”. I asked my father what the Prophet (S) had said after that and he told me that he had said: “All of them are from Quraysh.”
